claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
Adding approximately 2–4 at.% Al to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will promote formation of an alumina surface scale.
The alumina scale formed by the Al addition will be thin and continuous.
The alumina scale formed by the Al addition will adhere to the alloy.
Aluminum will preferentially oxidize to form stable Al2O3 under the stated exposure conditions.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The Al2O3 diffusion barrier will reduce oxygen ingress into the bulk alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress will prevent oxidation-induced embrittlement or mechanical degradation.
The Al-added alloy will exhibit significantly lower oxidation mass gain than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure.
The Al-added alloy will develop a thinner oxide scale than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr after exposure.
After exposure to air at 1000 °C for 100 hours, the Al-added alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within 8–16%.
After exposure, the Al-added alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed oxidation-resistance benefit applies around 1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere for exposure times up to approximately 100 hours.
The proposed mechanical-performance retention applies at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The conditions and boundary imply that mechanical loading at the specified strain rates may be maintained during the 100-hour oxidation exposure, whereas the falsification design exposes specimens first and performs tensile tests only after exposure.
